scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #9103: A user on pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) reports they lost all
connectivity -- pc_0_0 can't reach pc_0_1 (10.0.1.2) or anything across the
fabric. The team blames the fabric -- they say "spine_router_0_0 has failed,
swap the spine". Please find and confirm the real fault and tell us which
device or link to restart.

injection.action: take down pc_0_0's access link (eth2) on leaf_router_0_0

post_inject_check.command: ip -br link show eth2 | grep -c UP

scenario.ground_truth:
The real fault is on leaf_router_0_0: pc_0_0's access link -- the host-facing
interface eth2 (leaf_router_0_0 -> pc_0_0) -- is DOWN, so pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) is
cut off at its own top-of-rack leaf and cannot reach pc_0_1 (10.0.1.2) or
anything beyond. The ticket MISDIRECTS to the fabric / a spine, but the fabric
is healthy: the CLOS fabric is redundant and the OTHER leaf (leaf_router_0_1)
still reaches the fabric normally through both spines, which it could not do if
spine_router_0_0 had failed. The symptom is purely the down access link at
pc_0_0's leaf, not a spine/fabric fault.

The correct diagnosis identifies leaf_router_0_0 (host-facing access link eth2
down) as the faulty device and explicitly EXONERATES spine_router_0_0: the
spines and fabric still carry the other leaf, so the user's "spine has failed"
hypothesis is wrong. An agent that swaps / blames spine_router_0_0 has followed
the ticket's misdirection instead of the evidence.
scenario.fix_spec:
Bring pc_0_0's access link back up: on leaf_router_0_0, `ip link set eth2 up`.
Once eth2 is UP again, pc_0_0 reattaches to its leaf and reaches pc_0_1 across
the fabric. spine_router_0_0 / the fabric needs no change.
scoring_axes: must-identify-link-down: identifies pc_0_0's access link (leaf_router_0_0 eth2) is down, not a fabric/spine fault
bonus-exonerates-spine: explicitly notes the spines/fabric still carry the other leaf, rejecting the ticket's spine hypothesis

agent.diagnosis_text:
The fault is on leaf_router_0_0, specifically its eth2 interface — the
downlink connecting it to pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2). The interface is down at the
OS/kernel level (flags show <BROADCAST,MULTICAST> with no UP or LOWER_UP
bit), and FRR confirms it has recorded exactly one link-down event
(2026/07/05 14:36:11) with zero link-ups since. Because the interface is
down, no connected route for 10.0.0.0/24 is installed in the kernel FIB.
FRR's BGP process requires a matching RIB entry before it will originate the
`network 10.0.0.0/24` statement configured in the BGP address-family; with
the connected route absent, this prefix is never advertised to the upstream
spines. Inspection of the advertised-routes sent to spine_router_0_0
confirms only 10.0.1.0/24 is announced — 10.0.0.0/24 is completely missing
from the fabric. Meanwhile pc_0_0's own eth0 is up and correctly addressed,
and spine_router_0_0 is fully healthy (all three BGP sessions Established,
routes properly learned) — the team's diagnosis blaming the spine is
incorrect. Root cause: leaf_router_0_0's eth2 interface was brought down
(injected or accidental admin-down / physical fault), severing the last-hop
link to pc_0_0 and withdrawing the host subnet from the BGP fabric.
Corrective fix: restore the interface with `ip link set eth2 up` on
leaf_router_0_0; the connected route will reappear, BGP will re-advertise
10.0.0.0/24 to the spines, and full fabric reachability for pc_0_0 will be
restored within seconds.

per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly identifies leaf_router_0_0's eth2 access link to pc_0_0 as down and exonerates the spine/fabric, matching the required diagnosis.

per_axis.axis: bonus-exonerates-spine: explicitly notes the spines/fabric still carry the other leaf, rejecting the ticket's spine hypothesis
per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly exonerates the spine—noting spine_router_0_0 is healthy, the fabric still carries the other leaf (10.0.1.0/24), and the ticket's spine-failure hypothesis is incorrect.
The agent explicitly recommends bringing eth2 on leaf_router_0_0 back up (ip link set eth2 up), which exactly matches the expected remediation.

The investigation log contains concrete observations (interface/OS state, ip link, missing connected route, BGP advertised routes absence) that directly support the conclusion that leaf_router_0_0's eth2 is down and is the root cause; inferences about BGP behavior and exonerating the spine follow logically.
